follow100Note: Starbucks reports in tenths of a million; the figures on this page are rounded to whole $M.
footerNote: Reported operating income of $601M includes $59M of income from equity investees, shown here in Other income. Net earnings of $384M are essentially all attributable to Starbucks (noncontrolling interests absorbed a $0.1M loss).
oneTimers: Restructuring charges were $116M in the quarter as Starbucks simplified its global support organization under 'Back to Starbucks' — the main reason GAAP EPS of $0.34 sat below non-GAAP EPS of $0.41.
otherDetail: Income from equity investees of $59M and $28M of interest and other income, less $127M of interest expense.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Coffeehouses in the U.S. and Canada — comparable store sales fell 1%, with 4% fewer transactions partly offset by a 3% higher average ticket.

segments.name: International
segments.note: Coffeehouses outside North America — comparable sales rose 2%, with China flat as 4% more transactions offset a 4% lower average ticket.

segments.name: Channel Development
segments.note: Packaged coffee and ready-to-drink drinks sold in grocery and convenience stores — revenue slipped on a softer Global Coffee Alliance, partly offset by global ready-to-drink growth.

segments.note: Small leftover businesses and unallocated items.

takeaways.text: Global comparable store sales fell 1% on 2% fewer transactions, partly offset by a 1% higher average ticket. North America comps fell 1% (U.S. -2%); International rose 2%, with China flat.
takeaways.title: Comps were still negative

takeaways.text: Operating income fell 45% to $601M as store labor spending rose under 'Back to Starbucks' and $116M of restructuring charges landed. GAAP EPS halved to $0.34; non-GAAP EPS was $0.41.
takeaways.title: Investment and restructuring hit profit

takeaways.text: Starbucks opened 213 net new stores in the quarter, ending with 40,789 — 53% company-operated and 47% licensed. New stores helped revenue grow 2% to $8.8B.
takeaways.title: Still opening stores

verdict: Starbucks grew revenue 2% to $8.8B, but comparable sales fell 1% and profit halved to $384M as it spent more on store labor under 'Back to Starbucks' and took $116M of restructuring charges.
